content.user_title: Explore a Hazardous Alien Flora Expedition
content.value_statement: Writing a believable science-fiction research scene can be difficult when discovery, danger, and player choice must stay balanced. This skill provides a structured alien-botany chapter with dialogue, branching prompts, and narrative outcomes.
actual_capabilities: Presents a five-stage interactive story about researching alien plants.
Offers player choices for investigating glowing plants, giant trees, fruits, or ground plants.
Supplies fictional dialogue for scientific observation, classification, and field notes.
Introduces optional hazards involving a carnivorous plant or a harmful fruit.
Develops useful fictional resources such as insulation moss, rope vines, and medicinal sap.
Provides three ending directions for research success, caution, or mystery.
limitations: The skill is a fictional writing guide, not real botanical, medical, or survival advice.
Most content is written in Chinese with mixed English phrases.
It covers one chapter and does not generate a complete campaign structure.
Scientific details are speculative and require revision for hard science-fiction projects.

use_cases.title: Write an interactive chapter
use_cases.description: Use the staged dialogue and player choices to draft an alien-planet exploration scene.

use_cases.title: Run a roleplay session
use_cases.description: Guide players through research decisions, a small danger, and practical discoveries.

use_cases.title: Develop a science-fiction setting
use_cases.description: Adapt the plant behaviors and resource ideas into a broader planetary ecosystem.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Start the expedition
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Studying Alien Flora to begin Stella Chen’s alien-botany expedition. Present the four research options and wait for my choice.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Investigate light
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue the alien flora chapter. I choose the glowing plants. Write the observation sequence and keep Stella cautious and scientifically curious.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Add consequences
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chapter structure to create a new plant hazard. Include observable evidence, a safe retreat, and one plausible fictional research benefit.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Localize the narrative
prompt_templates.scenario: Adapt the chapter for a campaign.
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt Studying Alien Flora for my science-fiction campaign. Preserve the five stages, replace the plant names and ecosystem, and provide three ending hooks.

output_examples.input: Start the alien-botany expedition with the glowing plants.
output: Stella prepares her sample kit and examines the plant response to touch.
She records a possible light-storage mechanism and suggests a small, cautious energy experiment.

output_examples.input: Create an ending after a dangerous fruit experiment.
output: Stella recovers and documents the incident as a warning.
The chapter closes with a safer plan for classifying edible resources.

best_practices: State whether you want narrative, dialogue, or game-master guidance before starting.
Treat all plant effects as fictional unless you independently verify real-world information.
Use the hazard scenes to reward caution and observation rather than reckless choices.
anti_patterns: Do not present fictional medicinal or toxic plant details as real medical guidance.
Do not force a player choice when the scene asks for interaction.
Do not remove consequences from hazardous experiments, because caution is a central theme.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It provides an interactive science-fiction chapter about researching alien plants.

faq.question: What language is the source material in?
faq.answer: The source material is mainly Chinese and includes some English phrases.

faq.question: Is this real botanical guidance?
faq.answer: No. The plants, hazards, and scientific effects are fictional.

faq.question: Can I use it for tabletop games?
faq.answer: Yes. The choices and staged scenes can support a roleplay session.

faq.question: Does it include danger?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes optional fictional encounters with a carnivorous plant or harmful fruit.

faq.question: Can I adapt it to another setting?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace the plant details while retaining the discovery, hazard, and outcome structure.
